reviews.title: Perfect printer for a college student!
reviews.body: What's not to love about this great little printer? It does everything most people need—print, copy, and scan—in one compact unit.We've always been big HP printer fans, so we purchased this one for our granddaughter's college dorm room. She was able to set it up quickly on her own, and it worked perfectly right out of the box.The print quality is excellent, the wireless connection has been reliable, and its compact size is ideal for a dorm or apartment. If you're looking for an affordable, dependable all-in-one printer for a student or home office, this is an excellent choice.

reviews.author: BittersweetG

reviews.title: The troublesome program and the frustrating printing experience
reviews.body: I'm really at a loss for words. The printer itself is completely fine, but the program written by HP is a complete mess. The computer took a long time to finally print out a document, but then what happened? I happily threw away the packaging box, thinking everything was fine. But then what happened next? Damn it, the next day when I reconnected, I couldn't do anything. The port couldn't connect, and the program couldn't associate with the device. Later on, on the HP smart page, it showed that I was connected, everything was online, and everything was ready. Then I tried to open a random file from my Office 365 and print it. But it couldn't print out a single document. At this point, I thought, can't be! Maybe it's just an issue with Office. I never even thought to blame this HP printer. But I wasn't giving up. I opened a PDF file. Damn it, it still couldn't print. My computer was doing nothing. Alt+F4 didn't work either. I tried printing from the web. Haha, there was no sign of response at all. Who wrote this "WIRELESS PRINTING – Stay connected with our most reliable Wi-Fi, which automatically detects and resolves connection issues"? Was it written for someone else? For your boss? For your lover? For your mom? You can tell anyone "Oh, it's reliable", but you never told your own purchasing users. You used the most unreliable connection scheme! HP smart? Hp Stupid!!!! The connection program is long, complex, confusing, and no one knows why you have to register an account before you can connect. The network connection technology is even worse. Ha ha, do you know that the WSD port is inherently unreliable? Why didn't they design a backup port? And then you set WSD as the default option. I changed the option but they changed it back. I really can't stand it.Also, the designers never thought that not all networks are stable and long-lasting. Once they go offline or disconnect, this thing will be useless!!!The funniest thing is that downloading this program on a Windows system is a very slow process. During the download, I wasn't allowed to change the storage location. The design like this is like a sewage pit. Who should be buried for such a bad design? Why not something else? Because I suspect that the things that can be called organized in the design of this thing simply can't be sold for value! And that's not all. I tried using other built-in programs to print in an attempt to fix the bug. Damn it, you even won't let me use the most basic method. How can you be so proud of saying that the connection is reliable??? ?? ?

reviews.title: Ease and Quality ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
reviews.body: Everything was a breeze and I honestly can’t believe I did it! I have zero patience and I took a chance on this HP printer because my old printer was cabled internet and I wanted a wireless one but I was positive it was going to make me want to pull my hair out trying to get it connected. The whole set up was less than 20 minutes 🙏🏽☝🏽🩷!! I set it up with my phone first and then when it was connected to the WiFi, then my laptop was able to find it on the same network! There’s an option that goes one step further by allowing anyone connected on your WiFi the ability to print on that same printer. The printer doesn’t shake while printing and it also has a scanner that I’ve yet to test or try. I got this bad boy for under 40 bucks during a Prime day sale and if you ask me? It’s a steal. GET IT!

reviews.title: Great budget printer for everyday home use.
reviews.body: Great budget printer for everyday home use. I have been using the HP DeskJet 2855e for about three months now, and it has been perfect for my basic household needs. Setting it up through the HP Smart app on my phone was straightforward, and the wireless connection has remained steady on my 2.4 GHz network. I mostly print recipes, forms, and occasional school documents, and the text looks crisp and clean. The compact design is also a huge plus since it doesn't take up much room on my desk. The three months of free Instant Ink that came with the printer was a fantastic bonus, saving me from having to run out to buy cartridges right away. If you just need a simple, affordable all-in-one machine to print, scan, and copy at home, this is an excellent choice

reviews.title: Best Value on the Market
reviews.body: 4 STARS only because HP installation instructions are crap.  This is the fourth HP printer I have purchased in the last three years.  Number 1 was over $200.00, could never link to the internet with it.  Direct printing was successful 10% of the time.  Trashed it as the return time was exceeded.  HP instructions always seem to make reference to settings that you cannot find.  #2 was a cheaper version of #1, same result.  Number three was the same one as this purchase.  Kept getting a printer cartridge error, never resolved.  Returned (not to Amazon) and ordered from Amazon at a $20.00 price reduction but no shipping cost.  Well, things started happening...  Actually got test prints and info prints, but no file prints.  Pulled out a support document that had 22 steps to resolve problem.  Could not get past #5 because reference to a non-existent setting.  Finally, did pull down of print options.  Found a new one.  Hit it and VIOLA!  GREATEST LITTLE PRINTER UNDER $50.00 EVER!  PRINTER 5 STARS, HP SUPPORT 1 STAR
